symptom: After make-before-break replaces configured generation 1 with generation 2, configuration withdrawal leaves generation 2 and its ingress FIB state until shutdown.
root_cause: register.go::tunnelKey fixes LSPID=1. register.go::reconcileTunnels passes this configured key to reroute.go::teardownLSP, which removes exactly one generation and returns if it is absent. register.go::setupTunnel also looks up generation 1, so subsequent reloads can recreate it or update the wrong generation. Configuration reconciliation is not serialized with handleLinkDown's replacement creation.
owning_layer: RSVP-TE configured-tunnel reconciliation and generation lifecycle
workaround: Suppress head-end reoptimization or require the native fixture to reload before make-before-break finishes.
source_fix: Reconcile all ingress generations of the exact SESSION and sender identity, retaining bypass isolation. Select the current generation for ERO updates and retain the live predecessor when superseding an in-flight replacement. Serialize configuration reconciliation with received signaling and link-failure handling using the existing engine control lock.
why_not_workaround: Reoptimization is existing behavior permitted by RFC 4090 Section 6.5.2. Suppressing or racing it leaves the stale-generation product defect intact.

native_oracle: producer_integration_linux_test.go::TestRSVPNativeProducer marks capture immediately before config withdrawal, then requires a protected PathTear through bypass-a. The old repaired generation has already retired in attempt-011. RFC 3209 Section 4.6.4 permits switching to the accepted replacement and recommends tearing the old route; RFC 4090 Section 6.5.2 permits immediate reoptimization. RFC 2205 Section 3.1.5 requires tearing each corresponding path, and does not require a later replacement withdrawal to traverse the former repair bypass. The final protected-PathTear oracle is therefore not guaranteed after legitimate MBB. The fixture remains unchanged.
